page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The CPU architecture is 64-bit x86, featuring 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512 (specifically AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI), AES-NI, and BMI2, which assist with vector and cryptographic operations.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not included, requiring external block storage for persistent disk operations. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. It operates entirely on CPU execution, with no hardware GPU accelerators attached.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in lower performance tiers relative to modern cloud hardware. Synthetic compute evaluations record a Geekbench single-core score of 988.0 and a multi-core score of 2175.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 3616.07 and stress-ng multi-core metric of 2936.9, placing compute throughput in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth tests measure 21.08 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 18.75 GB/sec for writes. Compression benchmarks yield 19.17 GB/sec for gzip and 14.47 GB/sec for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, falling into the bottom decile. Application-level metrics reflect 2.88 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 3.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.g5.xlarge lies in its older microarchitecture and modest memory bandwidth, which constrain compute-dense or compression-heavy pipelines. However, its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio provides predictable dedicated CPU allocation without fractional throttling. This configuration fits basic enterprise utilities, low-traffic web serving, staging environments, internal development backends, and lightweight relational or in-memory caching tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a 2 Gbps network baseline. It contains no onboard local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage volumes. Across hardware benchmarks, the instance yields lower-tier performance metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 2175.0, a PassMark CPU score of 3616.07, and large-block memory read bandwidth of 21.08 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 2.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.36 GB/sec for static web serving. Featuring a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance, the ecs.g5.xlarge is designed for general workloads such as light web hosting, testing environments, background utility services, and modest caching deployments.
